---
title: "Florida Census Demographics: County and Tract Patterns"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

# Read clean Florida demographic and boundary data created by download_data.R
fl_census <- readRDS("data/fl_census.rds")
fl_tracts <- readRDS("data/fl_tracts.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: florida-choropleth
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-align: center

# Create choropleth map of Florida counties
ggplot(fl_census) +
  # Draw county polygons filled by Hispanic percentage with clean, crisp white borders
  geom_sf(aes(fill = hispanic_pct), color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  # Apply modern magma color palette with percentage labels
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    labels = label_percent(scale = 1, accuracy = 1),
    name = "Hispanic / Latino\nPopulation (%)"
  ) +
  # Clean map styling with no background clutter
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey30", size = 11, hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8.5, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 12)),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Hispanic Population Distribution in Florida",
    subtitle = "Percentage of county residents identifying as Hispanic or Latino (2018–2022 ACS)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2018–2022 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
  )
```

## Florida Tract-Level Data

Each dot below represents one Florida census tract. The plot uses tract-level
ACS estimates to show how median household income varies with the Hispanic or
Latino share of the population.

```{r}
#| label: florida-tract-points
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

fl_tracts_plot <- fl_tracts |>
  filter(
    !is.na(hispanic_pct),
    !is.na(med_incomeE),
    hispanic_pct >= 0,
    hispanic_pct <= 100,
    total_popE > 0,
    med_incomeE > 0
  )

ggplot(fl_tracts_plot, aes(x = hispanic_pct, y = med_incomeE)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1, color = "#2878B5") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  labs(
    title = "Income and Hispanic Population Share Across Florida Tracts",
    subtitle = paste(
      "One dot per census tract;",
      comma(nrow(fl_tracts_plot)),
      "tracts shown (2018–2022 ACS)"
    ),
    x = "Hispanic or Latino population (%)",
    y = "Median household income",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2018–2022 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Top 5 Counties by Hispanic Share

The table below highlights the five counties with the largest proportion of Hispanic residents in Florida:

```{r}
#| label: top-counties-table

# Prepare summary table of the top 5 counties by Hispanic share
fl_census |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(County = str_remove(NAME, " County, Florida")) |>
  arrange(desc(hispanic_pct)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  select(
    County,
    `Total Population` = total_popE,
    `Hispanic Population` = hispanicE,
    `Hispanic Share` = hispanic_pct
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `Total Population` = comma(`Total Population`),
    `Hispanic Population` = comma(`Hispanic Population`),
    `Hispanic Share` = percent(`Hispanic Share`, scale = 1, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  kable(
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = "Florida Counties with the Highest Hispanic Population Share"
  )
```

## Spatial Analysis

The choropleth map reveals a pronounced geographic concentration of Florida's Hispanic population, primarily clustered in South Florida and the Central Florida I-4 corridor. In South Florida, Miami-Dade County exhibits the highest Hispanic proportion in the state at 68.8%, reflecting historic and continuing immigration from Cuba and across Latin America, while agricultural interior counties like Hendry (57.1%) also sustain majority-Hispanic populations. Central Florida forms a prominent secondary hub centered on Osceola County (56.1%) and Orange County (32.9%), fueled by substantial inward migration of Puerto Rican communities to the Greater Orlando area. In contrast, northern Florida and the Panhandle exhibit significantly lower Hispanic population shares (often below 5%), highlighting a stark regional divergence across the peninsula.
